AN ACT to amend the executive law, in relation to redefining the term
"veteran"
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6159

SPONSOR: BROOKS
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the executive law, in relation to redefining the term
"veteran"

 
PURPOSE:

To update the definition of "veteran" to comport with the definition of
"veteran" in federal law, and to bring New York State's existing deliv-
ery of programs and services for Veterans and their family members into
conformity with federal law.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends Exec. Law § 350(3) to update the definition of veteran.

Section 2 renumbers various subdivisions of Exec. Law § 350.

Section 3 adds three new subdivisions 4, 5, and 10 to Exec. Law § 350 to
define the terms "combat veteran", "wartime era veteran" and "qualifying
service in Lebanon, Grenada or Panama".

Section 4 amends Exec. Law § 350(6) to update the definition of "armed
forces":

Section 5 amends Exec. Law § 357(1) to make a conforming technical
change.

Section 6 amends Exec. Law § 357(3) to require county and city directors
to be accredited as a veterans service organization representative with-
in one year of their appointment as director or acting director.

Section 7 amends Exec. Law § 358(1) to clarify that a VSA may provide
services to members of the national guard and reserve component of the
armed forces.

Sections 8, 9, 10 and 11 amend the Exec. Law to make a conforming tech-
nical changes to the definitions of veteran.

Section 12 amends Exec. Law § 369-h to update the definition of
"service-disabled veteran".

Section 13 would make the bill take effect immediately.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Articles 17, 17-A, and 17-B of the Executive Law, as enacted, contain
three very different definitions of "veteran." Each definition unneces-
sarily creates unfair or unreasonable burdens and qualifications that
limit or restrict the services that DVA and other state actors can
provide.

Article 17, Section 350, subsection 3 of the Executive Law requires that
an individual serve on active duty during wartime to receive recognition
as a Veteran under this section of the law.

Article 17-A, Section 369-b, subsection 3 of the Executive Law unneces-
sarily and unfairly limits the Veterans Employment Act to Veterans who
were released from service after September eleventh, two thousand one.

The proposed changes in Article 17-B, Section 369-h, subsection 7 of the
Executive Law bring the three (3) defmitions of "veteran" in the Execu-
tive Law into agreement, but makg no substantive change to the law or
increase the administrative burdens on any affected agency.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2017/18 - Senate S5373 (Croci) / A7800 (DenDekker)

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.
